project1.title: Lead-handoff orchestration
project1.problem: Inbound leads slipped between forms, CRMs, and inbox triage. First-touch SLA broke on 40% of nights and weekends, and weekend traffic was effectively a dead zone.
project1.solution: Single n8n pipeline normalized every inbound source, scored intent, routed to the rep on rotation, and posted a Claude-drafted opener into the rep's tool of choice — Notion for some, Airtable for others.
project1.result: First-touch SLA hit 99% across all hours. Inbox triage stopped being a job. Weekend conversion caught up to weekday.

project2.title: Content production pipeline
project2.outcome: Brief-to-publish time down from 6 days to under 36 hours
project2.problem: Briefs sat in Notion for days waiting for a writer, then waited again for editorial review, then again for SEO QA. Each handoff added a calendar day; the chain was longer than the work.
project2.solution: Claude with MCP read each brief, drafted a first pass against brand-voice memory, ran on-page SEO checks against a custom ruleset, and surfaced the result in Notion already flagged for the right human reviewer — writer, editor, or SEO lead.
project2.result: Brief-to-publish dropped to under 36 hours. Writers spent their time on the 30% that needed a human, not the 70% that didn't.

project3.title: Competitor intelligence loop
project3.outcome: Weekly competitor digest produced fully unattended; analyst hours redeployed to strategy
project3.problem: Tracking five competitors across pricing pages, release notes, and ad creative was a 4-hour Friday ritual for one analyst. Half the time the diff was trivial; the other half it mattered, and nobody trusted the eyeball method to catch it consistently.
project3.solution: Apify scrapers captured each surface on schedule, Python normalized the diffs into Supabase, and Claude wrote a short narrative every Friday morning naming what changed, what didn't, and what to investigate.
project3.result: Weekly digest landed unattended. The analyst stopped scraping and started reading; her time moved to the actual strategy work.

project4.title: Client reporting & dashboards ETL
project4.outcome: Monthly reporting effort per client cut from ~6 hours to ~20 minutes of review
project4.problem: Each account manager hand-pulled GA, Search Console, and ad-platform numbers into a deck every month. Three or four data sources, twelve clients, six hours each — and the deck still didn't tie out half the time.
project4.solution: Containerized Python ETL on Railway pulled every source on a schedule into Supabase, with a Google Cloud Run job assembling per-client dashboard snapshots. Account managers got a pre-filled draft with the numbers already reconciled.
project4.result: Monthly reporting collapsed to a 20-minute review pass. Numbers tied out. Account managers spent the recovered time on the conversation the client actually wanted.
